claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The unchanged alloy has poor load-bearing integrity, poor fracture toughness, and a tendency to crack.
The proposed intervention is a low-concentration Zr addition followed by controlled heat treatment.
Zr addition and heat treatment will produce uniformly dispersed, metastable tetragonal ZrO2 precipitates in the target alloy matrix.
Metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles partially transform to monoclinic ZrO2 under mechanical loading.
The mechanically induced ZrO2 transformation promotes crack-tip shielding.
The proposed crack-tip shielding processes include crack bridging, crack deflection, and crack branching.
Transformation toughening by the ZrO2 precipitates will enhance the target alloy's fracture toughness and load-bearing integrity.
The Zr-treated alloy will have more than a 20% increase in fracture toughness relative to the unchanged alloy.
The precipitates will not significantly alter microstructural features critical to the target alloy's caloric response.
The caloric response of the modified alloy will differ by less than approximately 5% from that of the unchanged alloy.
The intervention will preserve caloric performance under both applied magnetic-field and pressure-field operation.
The intervention will be effective over the typical caloric-device operating temperature range and service magnetic and pressure fields.
Extreme changes in field or temperature may alter the balance between mechanical and caloric properties.
Zr addition and ZrO2 precipitation might alter the entropy-driven mechanisms responsible for the caloric response.
Optimization of Zr concentration and heat-treatment parameters is needed to minimize adverse effects on caloric response.
